title: The Qur'an in your life
hook: You don't have to read the whole Qur'an this year. You just need to open it often.

screens.text: You already recite the Qur'an every day: al-Fatiha and a short surah in every prayer. Today is about making it a friend outside the prayer too, a few minutes at a time.
**Allah made it easy.** The Qur'an says it was made easy to remember [Q 54:17]. And it tells believers: *"recite what is easy from it"* [Q 73:20, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: The Prophet ﷺ said the best people are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it [Bukhari 5027].
That "learning" starts with one **ayah** (verse) at a time.

options.feedback: Right. Understanding the meaning matters, and someone who finds recitation hard gets a double reward [Muslim 798].

options.text: Reading a translation doesn't count for anything
options.feedback: Not quite. Understanding what Allah says is valuable. A translation is for understanding; recitation in prayer stays in Arabic.

options.text: He must master Arabic before opening the Qur'an
options.feedback: Not quite. Start with meaning now, and learn Arabic alongside, step by step.

steps.text: **Same time, every day.** Right after Fajr or before bed.
**Small.** Five minutes, or a few verses.
**Meaning and sound.** Read a translation, and listen to a reciter.
**Your surahs.** Review al-Fatiha and the surahs you pray with, so they stay solid.

cards.front: Do I have to learn to read Arabic?
cards.back: No. It's a bonus, not a requirement. But many converts find it opens up the Qur'an, and it's easier than it looks.
Most people learn the 28 letters in a few weeks of short practice. Reading smoothly takes a few months.
A beginner class at {{masjid.name}}, or a teacher {{mentor.name}} recommends. A teacher helps you get the sounds right.

screens.title: Five minutes with the Qur'an, right now
screens.intro: Optional: do it now if you have five minutes.

steps.text: Open a Qur'an app with a translation, or a printed copy (with wudu).
Pick one surah you pray with, like al-Fatiha or al-Ikhlas.
Read the meaning slowly, verse by verse.
Recite it once yourself. Before a ghusl that's due{women}, or on your period{/women}, listen along instead.
Choose your daily time for tomorrow and set a reminder.

screens.done_text: That's a Qur'an habit started. Same time tomorrow.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The Qur'an is made easy to remember [Q 54:17]; recite what is easy [Q 73:20].
- The best are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it [Bukhari 5027]. The one who struggles with it gets a double reward [Muslim 798].
- Translations are for understanding; recitation in prayer is in Arabic only (Q13).
- **Hanafi:** wudu is needed to touch a printed mushaf, and precautionarily a translation too [SeekersGuidance (touching a translation)]. Reading on a screen, or reciting from memory, is permitted without wudu, but not touching the verses on screen [SeekersGuidance (screen without wudu)]. Reciting is not permitted in major impurity (before ghusl) or during menstruation; listening, dhikr and du'a are fine.
- Learning the Arabic letters is optional and encouraged.

**Likely questions**
- *"Which translation?"* Saheeh International (used in this program) or another widely used modern English translation; ask the imam for a favorite. Read with a teacher or a brief commentary where possible.
- *"Where do I start after al-Fatiha?"* Short surahs at the end (the 30th part), or a surah the imam recommends; read with meaning.
- *"How do I learn the letters?"* A masjid class or teacher; 10 minutes a day; expect weeks for letters, months for fluency.
- *"Can I listen while I work?"* Yes, listening is fine; give it attention when you can.
- *"I'm on my period; can I read?"* In the Hanafi school, no recitation until it ends; she can listen, read the meaning on a screen without reciting, and make dhikr and du'a. Other schools differ; for details, the imam or a female staff member.

**Escalate:** detailed questions about recitation during a period or major impurity beyond the lesson; questions about tajwid rules (send to a teacher).

**Don't**
- Don't suggest reciting a translation in prayer.
- Don't set big targets ("finish the Qur'an this month").
- Don't shame anyone for not reading Arabic.
madhabNote: In the Hanafi school, reciting the Qur'an isn't allowed during a period or before ghusl after sex or a wet dream; the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools agree. The Maliki school allows a woman on her period to recite from memory. All four schools ask for wudu to touch a printed mushaf. On touching a translation, views differ even within the Hanafi school; the lesson teaches the careful view.
